23.0.0.en: 1 The word of the LORD came again unto me, saying, 2 “Son of man, there were two women, the daughters of one mother: 3 And they committed whoredoms in Egypt; they committed whoredoms in their youth: there were their breasts pressed, and there they bruised the teats of their virginity. 4 And the names of them were Aholah the elder, and Aholibah her sister: and they were mine, and they bare sons and daughters. Thus were their names; Samaria is Aholah, and Jerusalem Aholibah. 5 And Aholah played the harlot when she was mine; and she doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbours, 6 Which were clothed with blue, captains and rulers, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding upon horses. 7 Thus she committed her whoredoms with them, with all them that were the chosen men of Assyria, and with all on whom she doted: with all their idols she defiled herself. 8 Neither left she her whoredoms brought from Egypt: for in her youth they lay with her, and they bruised the breasts of her virginity, and poured their whoredom upon her. 9 Wherefore I have delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the Assyrians, upon whom she doted. 10 These discovered her nakedness: they took her sons and her daughters, and slew her with the sword: and she became famous among women; for they had executed judgment upon her.”

23.0.1.en: This is the third and last time in the Book of Ezekiel in which God accuses His people of the gravest unfaithfulness (chs. 16, 20, 23). Yet there is a difference between His accusation of His people in chapter sixteen and here. There He spoke of the unfaithfulness toward her heavenly Bridegroom in respect of her spiritual deviations; here He concentrated on the deviation of His people, in both its parts (Israel and Judah), in committing adultery through mistaken political thinking, that is, His people's reliance now on Assyria and now on Pharaoh of Egypt. This reliance carried, in the eyes of God, an insult to Him and a lack of faith in His ability to save them, and it also opened the doors of the Holy Land to receive pagan idols and their abominations from Babylon and from Egypt at that time.

23.0.2.en: God likened Israel and Judah to two sisters of one mother, who lived a life of adultery from their youth. The elder is called Aholah and the younger is called Aholibah. The first refers to Samaria (the capital of Israel) and the second to Jerusalem (the capital of Judah). The first is the elder because she comprises ten tribes, and the other is the younger because she comprises two tribes.

23.0.3.en: The two names are connected with the Hebrew word “ohel,” which means “tent.”

23.0.4.en: Perhaps He wanted to remind His people that in truth they ought to be the “tent” in which He dwells with His glory, to abide within it with them (Ex 33:7-10).

23.0.5.en: Perhaps by calling them thus He wanted to remind them of their sojourning on the earth, so that they would not settle in houses or fixed dwellings but in moving tents, to pass from one state to a better one, and from glory to glory. As Origen says: [He dwells in tents who runs toward God, free, without bonds or burdens.]

23.0.6.en: [If we ask: What is the difference between a dwelling and a tent...? A dwelling is something fixed and standing, with its fixed boundaries, but a tent is the dwelling of nomads who constantly move about; these find an end to their journeys.]

23.0.7.en: For this reason the Hebrews kept the Feast of Tabernacles (Lev 23:43) in remembrance of their dwelling in tents in the wilderness. As Origen says: [It befits each one of us, when he has come out of Egypt (the love of the world) and entered the wilderness, to dwell in a tent and to keep a feast in tents. Of what material must these tents be made, if not of the words of the Law and the Prophets, and the Psalms, and all that the Law contains?! When the soul grows by means of the Holy Scriptures, it forgets those things which are behind and reaches forth unto those things which are before (Phil 3:13); it leaves the lower places and grows and advances to what is greater. It grows in the virtues, and so changes its place of dwelling through its continual progress; in this way we can say that we dwell in the tent.]

23.0.8.en: Returning to the two sisters, we find them of one mother, since they were one people, and the two sisters fell together into adultery from their youth in Egypt. They shamelessly gave their bodies over to evil and so lost their spiritual virginity, and they opened their hearts to the idols of Egypt from their earliest beginnings (Ex 20:7). This was revealed in the wilderness when they made the calf of Apis and worshipped it in the absence of Moses on the mountain. As we said before in our commentary on the Book of Exodus, the absence of Moses was nothing but the touchstone that exposed the gods which the people carried secretly in their hearts.

23.1.0.en: Aholah (Israel) grew up, but she did not mature spiritually, nor did she take warning from her fall in Egypt; rather she inclined toward the young men of Assyria, clothed in blue, all of them desire, men of war, horsemen riding upon horses [5]. The Lord says, “she played the harlot when she was mine,” that is, she rejected Me as her Bridegroom and sought strange men for herself. She rejected the true heavenly Lord and desired those who were clothed in blue (a symbol of heaven), who pretended to religiosity while being earthly, sensual men full of fierceness. She rejected her Bridegroom who had fought for her in the land of her bondage, in the wilderness, and in her entering the Promised Land, and she imagined that the strangers, as horsemen, were able to protect her under the care of the king of Assyria, “that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand” (1 Kgs 15:19), and this was around the year 738 B.C. This reliance on Assyria led the latter to think of destroying Israel in 721 B.C.

23.1.1.en: The children of Israel did not rely on Assyria politically only; they also desired its gods and ran after its idols and its abominations, for it is said: “the children of Israel did secretly those things that were not right against the LORD their God, and they built them high places in all their cities... And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree... and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served Baal. And they caused their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, and used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do evil in the sight of the LORD, to provoke him to anger...” (2 Kgs 17). Therefore the Lord delivered them to those whom they desired, according to the desire of their heart, so they came under captivity and discovered their nakedness, that is, they came into disgrace and shame, and their sons and daughters were slain, and the children of Israel became like an unfaithful woman who tasted the bitterness of her unfaithfulness before all women, a warning and an example to them!

23.1.2.en: This is a living picture of the nature of sin and its working. It is deceitful and attractive; man runs after it, thinking that he will find in it bodily and psychological satisfaction, but it quickly brings him down beneath its feet, makes him lose his dignity, deprives him of his peace, and harms him bodily, spiritually and psychologically. Solomon the Wise described the work of the adulterous woman in the lives of those who fall into her snares thus: “[she] lieth in wait at every corner. So she caught him, and kissed him, and with an impudent face said unto him, I have peace offerings with me; this day have I payed my vows. Therefore came I forth to meet thee, diligently to seek thy face, and I have found thee. I have decked my bed with coverings of tapestry, with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt. I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us solace ourselves with loves... With much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him. He goeth after her straightway, as an ox goeth to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks; till a dart strike through his liver; as a bird hasteth to the snare, and knoweth not that it is for his life” (Prov 7:12-23).

23.2.0.en: 11 “And when her sister Aholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her inordinate love than she, and in her whoredoms more than her sister in her whoredoms. 12 She doted upon the Assyrians her neighbours, captains and rulers clothed most gorgeously, horsemen riding upon horses, all of them desirable young men. 13 Then I saw that she was defiled, that they took both one way, 14 And that she increased her whoredoms: for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with vermilion, 15 Girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in dyed attire upon their heads, all of them princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians of Chaldea, the land of their nativity: 16 And as soon as she saw them with her eyes, she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea. 17 And the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, and they defiled her with their whoredom, and she was polluted with them, and her mind was alienated from them. 18 So she discovered her whoredoms, and discovered her nakedness: then my mind was alienated from her, like as my mind was alienated from her sister. 19 Yet she multiplied her whoredoms, in calling to remembrance the days of her youth, wherein she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt. 20 For she doted upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses. 21 Thus thou calledst to remembrance the lewdness of thy youth, in bruising thy teats by the Egyptians for the paps of thy youth.”

23.2.1.en: The younger sister, “Jerusalem,” profited neither from the fall of her youth in Egypt together with her elder sister (before the division), nor from the experience of her elder sister Aholah, who ran after Assyria and worshipped their gods and fell into captivity. On the contrary, in the last period she filled up the cup of her evil more than Samaria had done before her, for the Lord says: “And when her sister Aholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her inordinate love than she, and in her whoredoms more than her sister in her whoredoms” [11]. Truly, after the division the kings of Judah appeared more holy than the kings of Israel, and when she went astray some reformers tried to remove the abominations, but she soon returned once again, in the days of Manasseh, to corruption in a more hideous manner than Israel had known in the days of its evil, and then this corruption extended over time. This chapter has made clear the features of this corruption:

23.2.2.en: A. Jerusalem doted on the Assyrians, the rulers, because of the magnificence of their clothing, which signifies the magnificence of their bodies and the grandeur of their appearance, together with their strength and their passions as young men; so she was deceived by these things like her sister. Jerusalem did not learn the lesson from Samaria, but did what was worse, for Ahaz, king of Jerusalem, sent to Pileser king of Assyria, saying to him: “I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, which rise up against me. And Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and sent it for a present to the king of Assyria” (2 Kgs 16:7-8).

23.2.3.en: B. There was no opportunity for the men of Assyria to seduce Jerusalem; rather Jerusalem sent to them, asking them to do evil with her, before she had seen them or met with them. She merely saw their pictures on the wall, and was dazzled by them at the glance of an eye. Evil had already become hidden in her heart. She runs to it and seeks after it; it is not evil that searches for her and tries to seduce her.

23.2.4.en: Young people sometimes fall into what they call love at first sight, or from the first meeting with a person of the other sex, and psychologists see in this love a kind of immaturity, because it is not based on intellectual study connected with the emotional side... It is only a decision taken by the inexperienced. But Judah did not fall into passion at the first sight, but through pictures on the wall!! She knows no maturity!!

23.3.0.en: C. The matter did not stop at her falling with Assyria, merely at seeing pictures of its men at the glance of an eye, but she also turned back to Pharaoh of Egypt, seeking evil as she had done before in her youth [19]. It is as though she were a hideous woman who asks for this one and runs after that one recklessly and without being satisfied. Here too there is a reference to reliance on Pharaoh of Egypt to deliver Jerusalem against Assyria, as King Zedekiah did.

23.3.1.en: A girl who loves a young man and declares to him that she has consecrated her whole heart to him alone, and then goes back to do the same thing with another behind the first one’s back, is counted a “flirt,” deceiving this one and that one... What if she did this with a young man and with his enemy at the same time? This is what the kingdom of Judah did in its relationship with Assyria and Pharaoh of Egypt!

23.3.2.en: Aholah represented a symbolic picture of the soul that sin has attracted and deceived; it was bright, beautiful and attractive, but deadly and fatal. Aholibah, on the other hand, represents the soul that runs after sin, seeking it without thought, in haste and without satisfaction, staggering to the right and to the left.

23.4.0.en: 22 “Therefore, O Aholibah, thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will raise up thy lovers against thee, from whom thy mind is alienated, and I will bring them against thee on every side; 23 The Babylonians, and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, and Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them: all of them desirable young men, captains and rulers, great lords and renowned, all of them riding upon horses. 24 And they shall come against thee with chariots, wagons, and wheels, and with an assembly of people, which shall set against thee buckler and shield and helmet round about: and I will set judgment before them, and they shall judge thee according to their judgments. 25 And I will set my jealousy against thee, and they shall deal furiously with thee: they shall take away thy nose and thine ears; and thy remnant shall fall by the sword: they shall take thy sons and thy daughters; and thy residue shall be devoured by the fire. 26 They shall also strip thee out of thy clothes, and take away thy fair jewels. 27 Thus will I make thy lewdness to cease from thee, and thy whoredom brought from the land of Egypt: so that thou shalt not lift up thine eyes unto them, nor remember Egypt any more. 28 For thus saith the Lord GOD; Behold, I will deliver thee into the hand of them whom thou hatest, into the hand of them from whom thy mind is alienated: 29 And they shall deal with thee hatefully, and shall take away all thy labour, and shall leave thee naked and bare: and the nakedness of thy whoredoms shall be discovered, both thy lewdness and thy whoredoms. 30 I will do these things unto thee, because thou hast gone a whoring after the heathen, and because thou art polluted with their idols. 31 Thou hast walked in the way of thy sister; therefore will I give her cup into thine hand. 32 Thus saith the Lord GOD; Thou shalt drink of thy sister’s cup deep and large: thou shalt be laughed to scorn and had in derision; it containeth much. 33 Thou shalt be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, with the cup of astonishment and desolation, with the cup of thy sister Samaria. 34 Thou shalt even drink it and suck it out, and thou shalt break the sherds thereof, and pluck off thine own breasts: for I have spoken it, saith the Lord GOD. 35 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; Because thou hast forgotten me, and cast me behind thy back, therefore bear thou also thy lewdness and thy whoredoms.”

23.4.1.en: Since Jerusalem was not restrained after seeing with her own eyes the captivity of Samaria her sister, but exceeded her in her immorality, the Lord used her lovers, Babylon and all the Chaldeans, especially the warlike tribes Pekod, Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians, to discipline her.

23.4.2.en: Pekod is an Aramaean tribe that lived in the plain east of the River Tigris, not far from its mouth (Jer 50:21).

23.4.3.en: Shoa is a Semitic name meaning “wealth,” the name of an Aramaean tribe dwelling east of Babylon, which was always at war with the Assyrians, and the Assyrians called them in their records “Sutu.”

23.4.4.en: Koa is a tribe that joined the Babylonians in the attack on Jerusalem, and it is probably the tribe called “Qutu” in the documents of the Assyrians, which lived east of the River Tigris.

23.5.0.en: Since she was fascinated by these tribes as men of war and captains of chariots [23], He delivered her to them to humble her when Babylon attacked Jerusalem and destroyed all her resources and disfigured all the beauty in her, for the Lord says:

23.6.0.en: “They shall take away thy nose and thine ears; and thy remnant shall fall by the sword: they shall take thy sons and thy daughters; and thy residue shall be devoured by the fire. They shall also strip thee out of thy clothes, and take away thy fair jewels. Thus will I make thy lewdness to cease from thee, and thy whoredom brought from the land of Egypt: so that thou shalt not lift up thine eyes unto them, nor remember Egypt any more” [25-27].

23.6.1.en: They cut off her nose, that is, her king, who ought to be at her head with the sense of discernment, so that he perceives the safe way and distinguishes it from the dangerous way. If he behaves badly and takes refuge with Pharaoh of Egypt against the king of Babylon, they cut him off from Jerusalem. As for us, the fruit of sin is our loss of the spirit of discernment by which we perceive the truth and reject falsehood, so that we live without tasting the truth and without grasping knowledge.

23.6.2.en: The cutting off of the ears refers to the captivity of the priests and the king’s counselors, who, instead of listening to the true prophets, listened to evil, false counsels and drove the people to destruction. So when we open our ears to vain counsels we lose our hearing of the voice of the Lord, like Eli the priest, who did not hear the call of God which the child Samuel heard.

23.6.3.en: As for the rest of Jerusalem, it falls by the sword, referring to the people who perish because of these actions. This signifies the body that is defiled and perishes because we are deprived of the grace of discernment and because we do not listen to the divine voice.

23.6.4.en: As for the burning of the sons and daughters in the fire, it is done by using them as human sacrifices to the god Bel or Molech. This is a reference to the squandering of the energies and talents that ought to have been offered for the glory of God and the edification of souls, which are used instead on behalf of Satan, for the destruction of the soul and the stumbling of others.

23.7.0.en: The stripping of her clothes and the taking away of her ornaments signifies her entering into public disgrace and shame before the Gentiles. This is the end of the sinner, who loses all his dignity and comes into shame before all, especially on the great day of the Lord, for He says: “thou shalt be laughed to scorn and had in derision” [32], as he becomes an example and a reproach after sin has utterly broken him.

23.8.s.en: 4. A concluding address to the two sisters:

23.8.0.en: 36 The LORD said moreover unto me; “Son of man, wilt thou judge Aholah and Aholibah? yea, declare unto them their abominations; 37 That they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands, and with their idols have they committed adultery, and have also caused their sons, whom they bare unto me, to pass for them through the fire, to devour them. 38 Moreover this they have done unto me: they have defiled my sanctuary in the same day, and have profaned my sabbaths. 39 For when they had slain their children to their idols, then they came the same day into my sanctuary to profane it; and, lo, thus have they done in the midst of mine house. 40 And furthermore, that ye have sent for men to come from far, unto whom a messenger was sent; and, lo, they came: for whom thou didst wash thyself, paintedst thy eyes, and deckedst thyself with ornaments, 41 And satest upon a stately bed, and a table prepared before it, whereupon thou hast set mine incense and mine oil. 42 And a voice of a multitude being at ease was with her: and with the men of the common sort were brought Sabeans from the wilderness, which put bracelets upon their hands, and beautiful crowns upon their heads. 43 Then said I unto her that was old in adulteries, Will they now commit whoredoms with her, and she with them? 44 Yet they went in unto her, as they go in unto a woman that playeth the harlot: so went they in unto Aholah and unto Aholibah, the lewd women. 45 And the righteous men, they shall judge them after the manner of adulteresses, and after the manner of women that shed blood; because they are adulteresses, and blood is in their hands. 46 For thus saith the Lord GOD; I will bring up a company upon them, and will give them to be removed and spoiled. 47 And the company shall stone them with stones, and dispatch them with their swords; they shall slay their sons and their daughters, and burn up their houses with fire. 48 Thus will I cause lewdness to cease out of the land, that all women may be taught not to do after your lewdness. 49 And they shall recompense your lewdness upon you, and ye shall bear the sins of your idols: and ye shall know that I am the Lord GOD.”

23.8.1.en: This address is considered a concluding speech which the Lord directs to the two sisters together, in which He reveals to them their evil clearly and declares its hideousness, whether in respect of abominations or the shedding of blood:

23.8.2.en: A. They committed marital unfaithfulness, for they left God and ran after idols, and then returned to defile His sanctuaries and profane His sabbaths, so they became worse than the Gentiles. Thus, when the believer goes astray, he mixes holy things with evil, and blasphemes the name of God and His holy things by his conduct.

23.8.3.en: B. They committed the most hideous kinds of barbaric crimes, such as offering their children as sacrifices to the god Molech, children who are the children of God.

23.8.4.en: C. They sent to men coming from afar to commit evil with them, adorning themselves with every ornament, and they used God’s incense and His oil in evil. It is as though they had not fallen by chance, nor as a result of seduction by others, but planned the scheme of evil themselves and used even the divine holy things to push others to commit evil with them.

23.8.5.en: D. They accepted from the rabble bracelets on their hands and a crown on their heads, instead of the gifts of God and His eternal crowns.

23.9.0.en: By this they deserved chastisement at the hands of those with whom they shared in the worship of their idols and abominations, and to whom they surrendered their bodies and their hearts, so that they would become an example to all, that they might not commit their atrocities [48]. Perhaps by this He meant that the Church of the New Testament, which came from the Gentiles, and which was Gentile and unfaithful, when she returned to God through faith in the Lord Christ and entered into a life of purity, would benefit from the lesson that was fulfilled in these two kingdoms of old.

23.9.1.en: Grant me to benefit from the falls of my brethren!

23.9.2.en: * Grant me to benefit from the falls of my brethren.

23.9.3.en: Samaria, the capital of Israel, fell, yet Jerusalem, the capital of Judah, did not benefit, for she thought she was above every law!

23.9.4.en: Instead of repentance she fell into abominations, and became more corrupt than her sister!

23.9.5.en: Teach me, O Lord, not to judge anyone, nor to gloat over anyone, nor to be proud, but to take warning from the falls of my brethren!

23.9.6.en: * I confess to You my weakness, and I cry to You asking for Your mercies.

23.9.7.en: Support me, and support my brethren!

23.9.8.en: Help me and help them, that we may all be saved and enjoy the fellowship of Your glories, O Lover of mankind!
